answer: In a Wesolowski VDF, each identity is checked by verifying a proof tied to repeated modular squaring, where every step depends on the prior result. An attacker may run cloned identities on separate GPUs, but cannot parallelize the sequential work of any one clone to evade its time cost; each requires its own computation. The yarrow, garden, and oasis serve as distinct challenge labels, not shortcuts around this physical bottleneck.
